text: Rootly’s Acknowledge, Snooze, and Escalate Alerts changelog describes an optional retrigger-acknowledged-alert setting: after ACK, a snooze timeout re-pages the same responder about an open alert. text: Grafana IRM’s response documentation warns that a new alert joining an acknowledged alert group does not trigger escalation-chain actions. Group-level acknowledgement therefore needs to be considered when checking whether a later alert obtained a fresh responder response. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

text: PagerDuty advances to the next escalation rule when nobody acts before its escalation timeout. Grafana Cloud IRM similarly escalates an alert that is not acknowledged or resolved within its configured timeframe. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)
keywords: Crypto bot alert acknowledgement and escalation evidence

text: An escalation chain is not a guarantee of eventual human response: Grafana Cloud IRM stops when all steps complete, and PagerDuty stops notifying after configured repeats and the final responder contact methods are exhausted. A bot monitor should test and expose this exhausted-chain outcome. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

text: PagerDuty documents a terminal escalation failure mode: when configured policy loops are exhausted, the incident remains assigned to the last user and stops notifying after cycling through that responder’s contact methods. text: PagerDuty snapshots the service escalation policy when an incident triggers and uses that version through its lifecycle; reassigning to the same updated policy records a new snapshot. text: In PagerDuty and Grafana Cloud IRM, acknowledgement indicates that a responder is investigating or working on an issue and stops automatic escalation notifications; it is distinct from resolution. A crypto bot monitor integrating these tools should therefore keep acknowledgement and resolution as separate states. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

text: Missing-ACK escalation depends on configured timeouts and fallback targets. PagerDuty advances through ordered rules if nobody acts before the timeout; the cited vendor’s routing article warns that a single schedule tier without fallback tiers can leave an alert unacknowledged. text: For response evidence, separate responder actions from message delivery: Grafana IRM exposes acknowledged/resolved times and records who manually advanced escalation; the PagerDuty case study in Google’s incident-response workbook uses a scribe ledger of actions, owners, and timestamps.
